purpose: Strengthen the unsigned matching-autarky kernel by the classical sign-aware linear-autarky cone. Show that nonzero z with A z>=0 yields an exact autarky and can be found by polynomial-time linear programming, then prove that on the canonical Tovey copy-cycle normalization the entire linear-autarky cone is exactly the replicated cone of the original 3-CNF. Thus the preprocessor is strictly useful in general but the copy-cycle source image does not manufacture new linear-autarky leverage.

signed_matrix.definition: For CNF F with variables x_1,...,x_n let A_F have one row per clause and one column per variable, entry +1 for a positive occurrence, -1 for a negative occurrence and 0 for absence. Assume no clause contains both polarities of one variable after tautology cleanup.
signed_matrix.rounding: For z in L(F), assign x_i=true when z_i>0, false when z_i<0 and leave x_i unassigned when z_i=0.

theorem_linear_autarky.name: NONZERO_LINEAR_CONE_VECTOR_GIVES_AN_EXACT_AUTARKY
proof: Consider a clause row a_C z>=0. If every variable of C has z_i=0, the rounded partial assignment does not touch C.
Otherwise, if every touched literal were falsified by sign(z), every nonzero contribution a_Ci z_i would be strictly negative, contradicting a_C z>=0.
Hence every touched clause contains at least one literal satisfied by sign(z). Therefore sign(z) is an autarky and all touched clauses may be deleted satisfiability-equivalently.
theorem_linear_autarky.polynomial_search: Because the cone is homogeneous, search for a nonzero vector by at most 2n rational LP feasibility calls A_F z>=0 together with z_i>=1 or z_i<=-1. If all are infeasible the cone is {0}. Repeating deletion at most |F| times yields a deterministic polynomial linear-autarky kernel with explicit witness lifting.

tovey_cone_isomorphism.setup: For each original variable x with occurrence copies x_1,...,x_k, the standard copy-cycle adds I_j=(NOT x_j OR x_{j+1}) cyclically. Let z_j be the linear-autarky coordinate of copy x_j.
tovey_cone_isomorphism.cycle_collapse: Summing the k inequalities gives 0>=0 while each says z_{j+1}>=z_j. Cyclic transitivity forces z_1=...=z_k=:w_x.
tovey_cone_isomorphism.inherited_rows: After this identification, the row inequality of every inherited clause is exactly the corresponding row of the original signed incidence matrix A_phi applied to w.
tovey_cone_isomorphism.theorem: L(red(phi))={R w : w in L(phi)}, where R simply replicates the coordinate w_x to every occurrence copy of x. Therefore red(phi) has a nontrivial linear autarky iff phi has one.
tovey_cone_isomorphism.assignment_alignment: The rounded signs of all copies of one original variable agree. Every implication-cycle clause is then satisfied whenever touched, and inherited-clause satisfaction is exactly the original linear-autarky condition.

positive: A deterministic polynomial sign-aware autarky reduction strictly stronger than unsigned matched-formula recognition in general.
Exact deletion with a concrete partial assignment and polynomial witness reconstruction.
A clean LP cone that can be run after the v4.6 matching-lean kernel.
source_return_firewall: Tovey copy cycles introduce no new linear-autarky directions: the cone is only a replicated copy of the original cone.
Therefore repeated matching plus linear-autarky preprocessing cannot claim progress merely because the bounded-occurrence encoding has many auxiliary implication clauses.
Any original linearly lean hard core returns as a linearly lean Tovey image.
not_killed: Nonlinear/global autarkies outside the linear cone.
A higher-order minimax or cancellation invariant on linearly lean cores.

next_target.name: E8_LINEarly_LEAN_NONLINEAR_GLOBAL_CONTRACTION_V4_8
next_target.directive: Run matching-autarky and linear-autarky kernels first. Attack only cores with no nonzero z satisfying A z>=0. Any next signed invariant must be genuinely nonlinear or higher-order; it must also survive the exact Tovey cone source-return identity and provide polynomial strict progress or an exact SAT/UNSAT terminal.

sources: Oliver Kullmann, Investigations on Autark Assignments, Discrete Applied Mathematics, 2000.
Marijn Heule and Hans van Maaren, Observed Lower Bounds for Random 3-SAT Phase Transition Density Using Linear Programming, 2004.
Handbook of Satisfiability, discussion of linear autarkies and polynomial decomposition.
